We discuss grammatical saturation, includinganalysis of the strongly connected components of the phrasal nonterminals in the Treebank, and model how, as sentence length increases,the effective grammar rule size increases as regions of the grammar are unlocked,yieldingsuper-cubicobserved time behavior in some configurations.This paper originated fromexaminingthe empirical performance of an exhaustive active chart parser using an untransformed treebank grammar over the Penn Treebank. Our initial experiments yielded the surprising result thatfor many configurations empirical parsing speed was super-cubic in the sentence length.This led us to look more closely at the structure of the treebank grammar.
